ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle AEC, point P is inside the triangle, and A, P, D are on the same straight line, with D on EC. At point A, an angle of 33° is marked; this angle is located between AE and the line from A passing through P and D. The problem text states that P is the incenter of triangle AEC. Reasoning: Because P is the incenter of △AEC, P must be on the angle bisector of vertex A, that is, AP bisects ∠EAC. In the figure, A, P, D are collinear, so AD and AP are the same angle-bisector direction. Therefore ∠EAD = ∠DAC. The figure gives ∠EAD = 33°, therefore m∠DAC = 33°.

raw_record.question_text: $P$ is the incenter of $\triangle AEC$. Find $m \angle DAC$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram: triangle AEC is shown, P lies on segment AD, and the marked 33° angle at A is the angle between AE and AD/AP. From the text, P is the incenter of triangle AEC. Since an incenter lies on the angle bisector of each vertex angle, AP bisects angle EAC. Because A, P, and D are collinear in the diagram, AD is the same angle-bisector line. Therefore angle EAD equals angle DAC. The diagram gives angle EAD = 33°, so m angle DAC = 33°.
